✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: A straightforward math and simulation problem that tests careful handling of repeated trips and edge cases. The main challenge is correctly counting the farm visits and return journeys while calculating the total shearing time.

Hi @CharlesNkdl!

There are still some parts of your clash that can be misleading. So in your statement, could you please clarify that:
1) The shepherd starts with the sheep.
2) This part - (to the farm and back to the sheep) - made me confused and I thought the whole journey from Sheep --> Farm --> Sheep was [[w]] minutes. I would rephrase it to this instead:
However, after every [[z]] sheep, he must take the wool to the farm then head back to the sheep. It takes him [[w]] minutes to travel the distance between the <<sheep>> and the <<farm>>.
3) "Once he finishes, he must go back to the farm anyway."
I would rephrase this to emphasize that this can be an edge case.
"If the shepherd is still with the sheep when he finishes shearing all [[x]] sheep, then he must return to the <<farm>> to finish his job."
4) In the input, change "sheeps" to "sheep".

Additional things:
- In all sections, please rename [[X]], [[Y]], [[Z]], and [[W]] to [[x]], [[y]], [[z]], and [[w]] as that is how the stub-generator generates the variables in the IDE.
- In your input/output sections, please add a space between Line and the number and also remove the space between the colon and number.
Example - Line1 : --> Line 1:

Thanks!

Goal
* Please format "X", "Y", "Z" and "W" as [[variables]] only and exclude other words from the formatting.

Input
* Is the variable in Line 1 [[X]] or [[N]]?

Output
* Please delete "N".

Constraints
* Test and Validator 3 violate the constraint on [[X]].

* Test and Validator 4 violate the constraint on [[W]].

Cases
* Some cases are the same. Please revise them so that every test and its validator cover the same scenario, but with slightly different inputs and outputs:

  • Test 3 and Validator 3

  • Test 4 and Validator 4

* Please remove the trailing newline from the input for Test 3.

Thanks.

Note that the plural of "sheep" is "sheep" instead of "sheeps" and I've changed that.

Test 4 still violates the constraint on [[W]]. Please fix the case or the constraint.

Thanks.

Good catch !
Done for W.
